artifacts_reviewed: PR #18 — 222-file rename + 34 git renames + 748 stale-ref claims
verdict_rationale: git renames preserve bisect-clean history; `git revert` restores all symbol names without data loss. The rename itself is mechanically reversible. The gap is ADR-0119: it lacks a Sunset/Reversal section (A2 violation), so the revert procedure is undocumented. No migration_rollback_script_path exists. Conditional pass pending F10-01.

findings.title: ADR-0119 omits Sunset/Reversal section — revert procedure undocumented
findings.evidence: A2 policy requires every ADR to carry a Sunset/Reversal section describing the revert trigger, revert command, and post-revert validation steps. ADR-0119 has no such section. Although `git revert <merge-sha>` is technically bisect-clean (git renames preserve ancestry), no documented procedure exists for: (1) validating that all 748 formerly-stale refs resolve correctly post-revert, (2) re-running the rename gate to confirm no dangling identifiers remain, (3) communicating the rollback to downstream consumers of the renamed crates.
artifact_refs: PR #18 — 222 file renames, 34 git renames, 748 stale-ref claims
findings.what_breaks_on_revert: Revert is mechanically clean. Risk is operational: without a documented validation checklist, a future reverter cannot confirm the 748 stale-ref resolutions are fully undone and no new dangling refs were introduced by the revert itself.
findings.remediation: Add Sunset/Reversal section to ADR-0119 containing: revert command (`git revert <merge-sha>`), post-revert gate command (re-run the rename/stale-ref CI lane), and a note that data_loss_class=none confirmed by bisect-clean git rename preservation.
